# DomAppendMovesNodeUnexpectedly

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Clone the node when preserving its existing parent. This inspection is disabled by default; enabling it selects the stated policy.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$d=new DOMDocument(); $a=$d->createElement('a'); $b=$d->createElement('b'); $n=$d->createElement('n'); $a->appendChild($n); $b->appendChild($n);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Clone the node when preserving its existing parent.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- The same proven node is appended consecutively to distinct proven parents. Enabling establishes that both parents must retain a copy. An intervening explicit detachment or clone excludes the finding (E3); do not infer this policy from identifiers.
- Resolve builtin functions, extension classes, constants and method receivers, including aliases and supported named arguments. Inspect reachable operations in one lexical scope with bounded local flow.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Never infer policy from names or comments. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Exclude shadowed or unresolved symbols, incomplete code, unknown required constants, ambiguous receiver identity and unsupported versions. Reassignment, escaping aliases, and unknown calls invalidate dependent flow facts.
- Both @custos-ignore DomAppendMovesNodeUnexpectedly and @noinspection DomAppendMovesNodeUnexpectedly suppress this native rule.
- E3. A call that executes on every path between the two appends counts as an explicit detachment when it is one of:
  - `remove()` or `replaceWith(...)` called on the node itself;
  - `removeChild` or `replaceChild` naming the node, positionally or through the `child`/`node` named arguments, on any receiver;
  - `replaceChildren(...)` called on the first parent;
  - `removeChild` or `replaceChild` called on the first parent with a removed child that is not proven to be another node. The removed child is proven distinct only when it and the appended node both resolve to different local allocation calls (`DOMDocument::createElement`, `createElementNS`, `createTextNode`, `createComment`, `createCDATASection`, `createDocumentFragment`, or `cloneNode`); `$parent->firstChild` and similar navigations are never proven distinct.

  The same calls on unrelated nodes or parents keep the finding, as does removing the first parent itself.

## Fix

None. A safe repair requires choosing values, error handling, or application behavior.

## PHP versions

Apply throughout PHP 5.3–8.5 only where the extension API and syntax exist.  Do not flag API unavailability through this rule. Legacy DOM classes are the initial target; modern Dom namespace classes require independently established matching contracts.

## Options

None. Use normal rule configuration to enable or disable the inspection.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DomAppendMovesNodeUnexpectedly": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DomAppendMovesNodeUnexpectedly
```
